questions.questionTextEn: For the gas-phase equilibrium $\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g)$, the equilibrium constants $K_p$ and $K_c$ are related by
questions.explanationEn: Here $\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$. Since $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$, we obtain $K_p = K_c(RT)^{-2}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Because a carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) molecule can adopt two nearly isoenergetic orientations ($\text{C}-\text{O}$ and $\text{O}-\text{C}$) in its crystal lattice at $0\text{ K}$, the theoretical molar residual entropy of solid $\text{CO}$ is
questions.explanationEn: By the Boltzmann entropy formula $S = k_B \ln W$, for $N_A$ molecules each having $2$ equally probable orientations, $W = 2^{N_A}$, so $S_0 = k_B \ln(2^{N_A}) = N_A k_B \ln 2 = R\ln 2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The excess pressure inside a spherical soap bubble of radius $r$ and surface tension $\gamma$ compared to the outside atmosphere is
questions.explanationEn: A soap bubble has two air–liquid interfaces (inner and outer surfaces). Each curved spherical interface contributes $\frac{2\gamma}{r}$, giving a total excess pressure $\Delta P = \frac{4\gamma}{r}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The limiting radius ratio ($r_{\text{void}} / R$) for a sphere to fit snugly inside a tetrahedral void formed by close-packed spheres of radius $R$ is
questions.explanationEn: From geometry of a regular tetrahedron, the limiting radius ratio for a tetrahedral void is $\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} - 1 \approx 0.225$ (while $0.414$ is for an octahedral void and $0.732$ is for a cubic void).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: According to the Gibbs phase rule, the number of degrees of freedom ($F$) at the triple point of a pure one-component substance is
questions.explanationEn: Using $F = C - P + 2$ with $C = 1$ component and $P = 3$ coexisting phases (solid, liquid, vapor), we get $F = 1 - 3 + 2 = 0$ (an invariant point).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For one mole of a gas obeying the van der Waals equation $P = \dfrac{RT}{V_m - b} - \dfrac{a}{V_m^2}$, the internal pressure $\pi_T = \left(\dfrac{\partial U}{\partial V_m}\right)_T$ is equal to
questions.explanationEn: Using the thermodynamic equation of state $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial V_m}\right)_T = T\left(\frac{\partial P}{\partial T}\right)_{V_m} - P$: here $\left(\frac{\partial P}{\partial T}\right)_{V_m} = \frac{R}{V_m - b}$, so $\pi_T = \frac{RT}{V_m - b} - \left(\frac{RT}{V_m - b} - \frac{a}{V_m^2}\right) = \frac{a}{V_m^2}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: One mole of an ideal gas expands isothermally at temperature $T$ from volume $V_1$ to $2V_1$ via two paths: (I) reversibly, and (II) irreversibly against a constant external pressure equal to the final pressure $P_2$. Comparing the magnitudes of work done by the gas ($|w_{\text{I}}|$ and $|w_{\text{II}}|$) and the entropy changes of the gas ($\Delta S_{\text{I}}$ and $\Delta S_{\text{II}}$), we have
questions.explanationEn: Reversible expansion gives maximum work: $|w_{\text{I}}| = RT\ln 2 \approx 0.693RT$, whereas single-step irreversible expansion gives $|w_{\text{II}}| = P_2(2V_1 - V_1) = \frac{RT}{2V_1}(V_1) = 0.500RT$, so $|w_{\text{I}}| > |w_{\text{II}}|$. Because entropy is a state function and both paths connect the same initial and final states, $\Delta S_{\text{I}} = \Delta S_{\text{II}} = R\ln 2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A binary liquid mixture of ethanol and cyclohexane exhibits a large **positive deviation** from Raoult's law ($\Delta H_{\text{mix}} > 0$). Such a mixture is expected to form
optionsEn: a minimum-boiling azeotrope with $P_{\text{total}} > x_A P_A^\circ + x_B P_B^\circ$
a maximum-boiling azeotrope with $P_{\text{total}} < x_A P_A^\circ + x_B P_B^\circ$
questions.explanationEn: Large positive deviations from Raoult's law occur when $A\text{--}B$ interactions are weaker than $A\text{--}A$ and $B\text{--}B$ interactions, yielding a higher total vapor pressure ($P_{\text{total}} > x_A P_A^\circ + x_B P_B^\circ$) and a **minimum-boiling azeotrope**.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a cubic crystal of lattice parameter $a$, the ratio of the interplanar spacing $d_{111}$ to $d_{200}$ is
questions.explanationEn: For a cubic lattice, $d_{hkl} = \frac{a}{\sqrt{h^2 + k^2 + l^2}}$. Hence $d_{111} = \frac{a}{\sqrt{3}}$ and $d_{200} = \frac{a}{2}$, giving $\frac{d_{111}}{d_{200}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about dilute solutions of non-volatile solutes is/are correct?
optionsEn: The ebullioscopic constant $K_b$ depends on the nature of the solvent and not on the identity of the solute.
Osmotic pressure is preferred for determining molar masses of macromolecules (like proteins and polymers) because it yields measurable pressure even at very low molarities.
At the same molality in water, $0.01\text{ m}$ $\text{AlCl}_3$ produces a larger freezing point depression than $0.01\text{ m}$ urea.
Adding a non-volatile solute to a pure solvent increases the chemical potential of the solvent.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** $K_b = \frac{R T_b^{*2} M_1}{1000 \Delta H_{\text{vap}}}$ is purely a solvent property.
- **(B) True:** $\Pi = CRT$ is large enough to measure accurately for dilute macromolecular solutions.
- **(C) True:** $\text{AlCl}_3$ dissociates ($i \approx 4$) vs. urea ($i = 1$).
- **(D) False:** $\mu_1 = \mu_1^* + RT\ln x_1 < \mu_1^*$, so adding a solute *lowers* the solvent's chemical potential.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a reversible Carnot heat engine operating between temperatures $T_h$ (hot) and $T_c$ (cold) with $T_h > T_c > 0$, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: The efficiency depends only on $T_h$ and $T_c$, and not on the working substance.
The net entropy change of the working substance over one complete cycle is zero.
The net entropy change of the universe over one complete cycle is zero.
The efficiency can reach $100\%$ for finite $T_h$ and $T_c > 0$.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A), (B), (C) True:** Carnot efficiency $\eta = 1 - T_c/T_h$ is universal; $S$ is a state function ($\Delta S_{\text{sys}} = 0$); and because all steps are reversible, $\Delta S_{\text{univ}} = 0$.
- **(D) False:** $\eta = 1$ requires $T_c = 0\text{ K}$, which is unattainable by the Third Law.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about a Joule–Thomson throttling expansion of a gas is/are correct?
optionsEn: The process occurs at constant enthalpy ($\Delta H = 0$).
For an ideal gas, the Joule–Thomson coefficient $\mu_{\text{JT}} = \left(\dfrac{\partial T}{\partial P}\right)_H$ is identically zero.
A real gas cools upon throttling when $\mu_{\text{JT}} > 0$ (below its inversion temperature).
The Joule–Thomson expansion is a reversible, isentropic ($\Delta S = 0$) process.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** Throttling through a porous plug is isenthalpic ($\Delta H = 0$).
- **(B) True:** For an ideal gas, $H = H(T)$ only, so $\mu_{\text{JT}} = 0$.
- **(C) True:** Since $\Delta P < 0$ during expansion, $\Delta T = \mu_{\text{JT}}\Delta P < 0$ (cooling) when $\mu_{\text{JT}} > 0$.
- **(D) False:** Throttling is inherently irreversible with $\Delta S > 0$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a reaction with $\Delta H^\circ = +40.0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta S^\circ = +100.0\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, the value of $\Delta G^\circ$ at $500\text{ K}$ is _______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Using $\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ = 40.0 - 500(0.100) = 40.0 - 50.0 = -10\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The maximum possible coefficient of performance ($\text{COP} = \dfrac{T_c}{T_h - T_c}$) of a Carnot refrigerator operating between a cold compartment at $250\text{ K}$ and a room at $300\text{ K}$ is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: For an ideal Carnot refrigerator, $\text{COP} = \frac{T_c}{T_h - T_c} = \frac{250}{300 - 250} = \frac{250}{50} = 5$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: X-rays of wavelength $1.50\text{ \AA}$ undergo second-order ($n = 2$) Bragg diffraction from crystal planes with interplanar spacing $d = 3.00\text{ \AA}$. The Bragg angle $\theta$ is _______ degrees. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: By Bragg's law, $\sin\theta = \frac{n\lambda}{2d} = \frac{2 \times 1.50}{2 \times 3.00} = 0.50 \implies \theta = 30^\circ$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of tetrahedral voids completely contained within one face-centered cubic (fcc) unit cell is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: An fcc unit cell contains $Z = 4$ atoms. Since there are $2$ tetrahedral voids per close-packed atom, one fcc unit cell contains $2 \times 4 = 8$ tetrahedral voids (one in each octant).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a van der Waals gas with excluded volume constant $b = 42.0\text{ cm}^3\text{ mol}^{-1}$, the critical molar volume $V_{m,c}$ is _______ $\text{cm}^3\text{ mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: For a van der Waals gas, $V_{m,c} = 3b = 3 \times 42.0 = 126\text{ cm}^3\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn:
For $\text{CO}_2$, the van der Waals constants are $a = 0.365\text{ Pa m}^6\text{ mol}^{-2}$ and $b = 4.27 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}^3\text{ mol}^{-1}$. Its critical temperature $T_c$ is _______ $\text{K}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
[Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: Using $T_c = \frac{8a}{27Rb} = \frac{8 \times 0.365}{27 \times 8.314 \times 4.27 \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{2.92}{9.5852 \times 10^{-3}} \approx 304.6\text{ K}$.
